# Dhātu Sutta (Iti 51 (It 3.2 PTS It 45))

**ID:** Iti 51 (It 3.2 PTS It 45)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Dhātu Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0504m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhātu Sutta* (Iti 51; It 3.2, PTS It 45), also titled the *Dhātusutta* and translated as "Elements", is a short discourse from the *Tikanipāta* section of the *Itivuttaka*. The sutta expounds three basic properties or elements (*dhātu*): the element of form (*rūpadhātu*), the formless element (*arūpadhātu*), and the element of cessation (*nirodhadhātu*). In the accompanying verse portion, those who fully comprehend the form element, do not cling to the formless realms, and find release in cessation are said to leave death behind; having personally experienced the deathless realm and realized the "relinquishing of all acquisitions" (*upadhipaṭinissagga*), the uncorrupted (*anāsavo*) Buddha teaches this sorrowless, unsoiled state [de La Vallée Poussin 1923]. Louis de La Vallée Poussin cited this specific verse occurrence of *upadhipaṭinissagga* in his commentary on the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* as a direct canonical Pali counterpart to the Sanskrit Nirvāṇa formula *sarvopadhipratiniḥsarga* [de La Vallée Poussin 1923].
